cohort: The study included 400 term pregnant women with cephalic singleton pregnancies and spontaneous onset of labor.
finding: The incidence of nuchal cord was 21.25%, with multiple and tight loops significantly associated with prolonged labor, abnormal fetal heart rate patterns, lower 1-minute APGAR scores, and higher rates of NICU admission.
mod_finding: Abnormal fetal heart rate patterns, more common in multiple and tight cord cases, led to increased instrument-assisted deliveries (forceps and cesarean section).
followup_time: Immediate neonatal period (APGAR scores at 1 and 5 minutes, NICU admissions)
